chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Sa'id ibn Amr al-Ju'fi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) one day while he was eating while leaning (upon something). He said: 'And it had reached us that this is disliked.' So I began looking at him, and he invited me to his food. When he had finished, he said: 'O Muhammad, perhaps you think that no eye saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) eating while he was leaning from the time Allah sent him until He took him.' He said: 'Then he corrected himself and said: No, by Allah, no eye saw him eating while he was leaning from the time Allah sent him until He took him.'

Then he said: 'O Muhammad, perhaps you think that he was satisfied with wheat bread for three consecutive days from the time Allah sent him until He took him.' Then he corrected himself, then said: 'No, by Allah, he was not satisfied with wheat bread for three consecutive days since Allah sent him until He took him. Indeed, I do not say that he could not find it; he used to gift one man a hundred camels. So if he had intended to eat it, he would have eaten.'

And Jibril (peace be upon him) had come to him with the keys of the treasures of the earth three times, giving him the choice, without Allah, Blessed and Exalted, deducting anything from what Allah had prepared for him on the Day of Resurrection. So he chose modesty to his Lord, Glorified and Exalted.

And whenever he was asked for anything, he never said 'No'. If he had given, he would say 'Yes'; if he had not, he would say 'It will be'. And whatever he gave to Allah, he never failed to deliver it to him, to the extent that if he gave a man Paradise, Allah would deliver that to him.

Then he reached out to me with his hand and said: 'And indeed, your Master (Ali) used to sit with the sitting of a slave, and eat with the eating of a slave, and feed the people with wheat bread and meat, and would return to his family to eat bread and oil.'

And if he were to buy a Sunbulani shirt, he would let his slave choose the better of the two, then wear the remaining one. So if it exceeded his fingers, he would cut it, and if it exceeded his heel, he would remove it.
And no two matters ever came to him, both for the sake of Allah's pleasure, except that he would take the more difficult of the two upon his body.

And indeed, he was the ruler of the people for five years, but he did not place a brick upon a brick, nor a baked brick upon a baked brick, nor acquire a piece of land, nor leave a legacy of white or red (coins) except seven hundred dirhams that remained from his gifts, intending that he would buy a servant for his family with them.

And no one could bear his work, and indeed Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) would look into the Book from the books of Ali (peace be upon him), so he would strike the ground with it and say: 'Who can endure this?'
ai.seo_question: What were the eating and lifestyle habits of the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Prophet’s avoidance of reclining while eating and his limited consumption of wheat bread were acts of voluntary asceticism (zuhd) rather than necessity, as he possessed the keys to the earth’s treasures. This narration highlights the prophetic model of balancing spiritual humility with worldly capability, a theme further exemplified by the description of Imam Ali’s governance, where he accumulated no personal wealth despite ruling for five years. The hadith serves as a theological counter to the notion that the Prophet’s simplicity stemmed from poverty, emphasizing instead his conscious choice of modesty to remain close to his Lord.
